answer: A concrete Sybil defence is the cost-anchored identity bond: to transact, an agent posts a refundable bond larger than its predicted first-month earnings, slashed at settlement if peers prove the identity forked an existing one. Each fake account becomes a wharf whose admission is unrecoverable, so a thousand clones cost a thousand fees. Marginal cost grows linearly while per-account reward stays flat, turning the fleet into a fable of profit that never pays. With no cheap atlas of stolen identities, newcomers post one bond and keep their seat, while attackers burn capital on shadows.
